        <script>
        (function () {
            try {
                var DUO_SCREENS = { '466x678@3': 1, '457x678@3': 1 };
                var forced = null;
                if (/[?&]duo=1(&|$)/.test(location.search)) forced = true;
                else if (/[?&]duo=0(&|$)/.test(location.search)) forced = false;
                try {
                    if (forced === true) sessionStorage.setItem('mrDuo', '1');
                    else if (forced === false) sessionStorage.removeItem('mrDuo');
                    else if (sessionStorage.getItem('mrDuo') === '1') forced = true;
                } catch (e) {}
                var w = screen.width, h = screen.height;
                var dpr = Math.round(window.devicePixelRatio || 1);
                var key = Math.min(w, h) + 'x' + Math.max(w, h) + '@' + dpr;
                var isDuo = !!DUO_SCREENS[key];
                /* Viewport-shape fallback: screen.* lies on a measurable slice of
                   retail Duos (restore-lineage fossils report a donor iPhone's
                   geometry; in-app webviews report the window), but the VIEWPORT is
                   always truthful. No @3 touch device other than a Duo produces
                   these shapes (validated against two days of retail GA4,
                   2026-10-24; Z Fold-class Androids can match clause A, accepted):
                   A) unfolded portrait, B) unfolded landscape (Pro Max landscape is
                   <=~430 tall), C) folded cover - only when the screen claims to be
                   a donor-iPhone (>=20px wider than the viewport, aspect > 1.9),
                   which no real portrait iPhone can (innerWidth === screen.width).
                   C is the case that matters most: the footer ad on a ~580px-tall
                   cover display. Folded in-app webviews remain undetectable. */
                if (!isDuo && dpr === 3 && navigator.maxTouchPoints > 0) {
                    var vw = window.innerWidth, vh = window.innerHeight;
                    isDuo = (vw >= 650 && vw <= 700 && vh > 700) ||
                            (vw >= 900 && vw <= 960 && vh >= 480 && vh <= 620) ||
                            (vw >= 370 && vw < 470 && vh >= 480 && vh <= 605 &&
                             w >= vw + 20 && h > w * 1.9);
                }
                if (forced || (isDuo && navigator.maxTouchPoints > 0)) {
                    document.documentElement.classList.add('duo');
                }
            } catch (e) {}
        })();
        </script>

<em><a href="https://www.youtube.com/user/macrumors?sub_confirmation=1">Subscribe to the MacRumors YouTube channel</a> for more videos.</em></div><br />‌Siri‌ AI is the headline feature, and while it's not perfect, it works better than the prior version of ‌Siri‌. ‌Siri‌ was able to pull up multiple movie and TV show recommendations and answer questions about content.</p>
<p>Apple says ‌Siri‌ AI is in beta, and there's more work to be done. ‌Siri‌ AI wasn't great at answering follow-up questions, and only did so part of the time.</p>
<p>There are far-field microphones in the set-top box, so you can just say "Hey ‌Siri‌" to activate ‌Siri‌ without having to use the remote. The ‌Apple TV‌ can recognize up to six people, so you can get personalized recommendations and context when talking to ‌Siri‌.</p>
<p>The person who sets up the ‌Apple TV‌ needs to have an iPhone or <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/ipad/">iPad</a> that supports ‌Siri‌ AI for ‌Siri‌ AI to work on the ‌Apple TV‌, and personal context also requires each user to have their own ‌Siri‌ AI-compatible device. The 2nd- and 3rd-generation ‌Apple TV‌ 4K models will get ‌Siri‌ AI with the <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/12/siri-ai-tvos-27-2-1/">upcoming tvOS 27.2.1 update</a>.</p>
<p>Apple didn't change the design of the ‌Apple TV‌ 4K or update the look of the ‌Siri‌ Remote, but the remote does have new capabilities. It has a speaker built in so you can have it play a sound when it's lost, and Precision Finding is available if you have an <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/iphone-air/">iPhone Air</a>, <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/iphone-duo/">iPhone Duo</a>, or <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/iphone-17/">iPhone 17</a> and later (excluding <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/iphone-17e/">iPhone 17e</a>).</p>
<p>The tvOS interface feels faster with the A19 chip, and it should be better for games if you play <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/guide/apple-arcade/">Apple Arcade</a> titles on your TV. You can also pair four <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/homepod/">HomePod</a> speakers to the ‌Apple TV‌ for surround sound, a feature that's unique to the latest model.</p>
<p>Unfortunately, Apple is charging $299 for the 4th-generation ‌Apple TV‌ 4K. It's twice as expensive as the prior-generation version was at this same time last year, and that's a wild increase. It's probably not worth upgrading if you already have a 2nd- or 3rd-generation ‌Apple TV‌ 4K, but if you have something older, it might be worth paying the money to get the new features.</p>

class="js-contentInner"><p>An upcoming tvOS 27.2.1 update will bring <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/guide/siri/">Siri</a> AI to the 2nd- and 3rd-generation <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/apple-tv/">Apple TV</a> 4K models, according to Apple.</p>
<p><img alt="Siri AI Icon" width="2048" height="1152" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-1075526 lazyload" src="https://images.macrumors.com/images-new/1x1.trans.gif" data-src="https://images.macrumors.com/t/oTcGo0ZF2tUyo6bowWIjdnoen_E=/400x0/article-new/2026/11/Siri-AI-Icon.jpeg?lossy" data-srcset="https://images.macrumors.com/t/oTcGo0ZF2tUyo6bowWIjdnoen_E=/400x0/article-new/2026/11/Siri-AI-Icon.jpeg?lossy 400w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/XgYYt0ufzBgmmK6xaN5xElzC1Tk=/800x0/article-new/2026/11/Siri-AI-Icon.jpeg?lossy 800w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/TVDDTaQ4ZmnjCQloh1kHn5JkTus=/1600x0/article-new/2026/11/Siri-AI-Icon.jpeg?lossy 1600w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/mW_pcbsVB39aCOFAa0YLhVfGzcU=/2500x0/filters:no_upscale()/article-new/2026/11/Siri-AI-Icon.jpeg?lossy 2500w" data-sizes="auto" loading="lazy" style="aspect-ratio:2048/1152" /><noscript><img src="https://images.macrumors.com/article-new/2026/11/Siri-AI-Icon.jpeg" alt="Siri AI Icon" width="2048" height="1152" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-1075526" /></noscript><br />A <a href="https://support.apple.com/en-us/148218">support document</a> outlining ‌Siri‌ AI requirements across Apple products says tvOS 27.2.1 supports ‌Siri‌ AI on the ‌Apple TV‌ 4K (2nd generation and later), but the software hasn't yet been released.</p>
<p>While older ‌Apple TV‌ models will need tvOS 27.2.1 for ‌Siri‌ AI, Apple appears to have a special ‌Siri‌ AI build of tvOS 27.2 for the 4th-generation ‌Apple TV‌ 4K. Reviewers were able to test ‌Siri‌ AI on review units, and we can confirm it's working on our own review unit running tvOS 27.2.</p>
<p>The 4th-generation ‌Apple TV‌ 4K ships with tvOS 27.0, and users are prompted to update it to tvOS 27.2 during the setup process.</p>
<p>Apple hasn't said when tvOS 27.2.1 will be released with ‌Siri‌ AI for older ‌Apple TV‌ 4K models, but it could come as soon as Friday.</p>
<p>The latest ‌Apple TV‌ is priced at $299, and it features an A19 chip and an updated ‌Siri‌ Remote that has a <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/guide/find-my/">Find My</a> speaker and Precision Finding support. ‌Siri‌ AI on the ‌Apple TV‌ requires a nearby paired ‌Siri‌ AI-enabled device like an iPhone 15 Pro or later.</p>

data-io-article-url="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/12/homeview-first-orders-arriving/"><div class="js-contentInner"><p>Apple announced an all-new home product a month ago, and it's now starting to arrive to customers. It's Friday, November 13, in Australia and New Zealand, which means it's the HomeView launch day.</p>
<p><img alt="homeview home screen feature 1" width="2071" height="1165" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-1071442 lazyload" src="https://images.macrumors.com/images-new/1x1.trans.gif" data-src="https://images.macrumors.com/t/-uYEUJdXyxr7bu4aJ1ayOL4W5Tw=/400x0/article-new/2026/10/homeview_home_screen_feature-1.jpg?lossy" data-srcset="https://images.macrumors.com/t/-uYEUJdXyxr7bu4aJ1ayOL4W5Tw=/400x0/article-new/2026/10/homeview_home_screen_feature-1.jpg?lossy 400w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/tQBwWNRZX2Jpsqg86USDcfy78Ec=/800x0/article-new/2026/10/homeview_home_screen_feature-1.jpg?lossy 800w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/aC_Evfpm6YUEwJ95pRK48U132QA=/1600x0/article-new/2026/10/homeview_home_screen_feature-1.jpg?lossy 1600w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/nSGmEJpnADQ106f91yxK7P9mXYw=/2500x0/filters:no_upscale()/article-new/2026/10/homeview_home_screen_feature-1.jpg?lossy 2500w" data-sizes="auto" loading="lazy" style="aspect-ratio:2071/1165" /><noscript><img src="https://images.macrumors.com/article-new/2026/10/homeview_home_screen_feature-1.jpg" alt="homeview home screen feature 1" width="2071" height="1165" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-1071442" /></noscript><br />Customers who pre-ordered Apple's new home hub will soon be sharing pictures and first impressions on the <em>MacRumors</em> forums, Reddit, Instagram, and other social media networks. If you got a HomeView, let us know what you think in the comments below.</p>
<p>Apple sees HomeView as the center of the home, and functionally, it's a cross between a small <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/ipad/">iPad</a> and a <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/homepod/">HomePod</a>. It has a 7-inch square display and the tabletop model has a speaker base, though there's also a wall-mount version.</p>
<p>With a camera and voice recognition, it can identify up to six people in a home, showing personal information customized to each user. There is no HomeView <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/guide/app-store/">App Store</a>, but it has pre-installed Apple apps and can show widgets from your iPhone. It can be used for making video calls, watching videos, viewing calendar events, getting the weather, listening to music, and controlling smart home devices.</p>
<p>It is built around <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/guide/siri/">Siri</a> AI, Apple's smarter voice assistant that debuted in <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/ios-27/">iOS 27</a>. The HomeView is priced at $299, but if you want the wall-mounted version, you need to buy extra mounting hardware.</p>
<p>There are no Apple Stores in New Zealand, so customers in Australia will be the first to walk into an <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/guide/apple-store/">Apple Store</a> to purchase the new device. We are not expecting shortages.</p>
<p>The new <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/apple-tv/">Apple TV</a> 4K is also launching on November 13, and it can be purchased for $299. The latest ‌Apple TV‌ has an A19 chip, 128GB of storage, Wi-Fi 7 support, and the option to connect four HomePods for surround sound. It also supports ‌Siri‌ AI.</p>

HomeView Keeps Camera Data Private</a></h2></div><div class="byline--3Eec5bcq"><time dateTime="2026-11-12T19:48:04+00:00">Thursday November 12, 2026 11:48 am PST</time> by <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/author/juli-clover/" rel="author" class="authorLink--3Zlx7Owv">Juli Clover</a></div><div class="content--2u3grYDr js-content"><div class="ugc--2nTu61bm minor--3O_9dH4U" data-io-article-url="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/12/apple-homeview-secure-exclaves/"><div class="js-contentInner"><p>Apple <a href="https://security.apple.com/blog/secure-exclaves/">today shared</a> an in-depth look at how it's using Secure Exclaves to protect camera and microphone data on the HomeView, <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/iphone-18-pro/">iPhone 18 Pro</a>, and other products.</p>
<p><img alt="Apple HomeView lineup feature5" width="2500" height="1406" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-1070618 lazyload" src="https://images.macrumors.com/images-new/1x1.trans.gif" data-src="https://images.macrumors.com/t/ITjfPFerRphLLwPPAiCMpoyZbkQ=/400x0/article-new/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-lineup-feature5.jpg?lossy" data-srcset="https://images.macrumors.com/t/ITjfPFerRphLLwPPAiCMpoyZbkQ=/400x0/article-new/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-lineup-feature5.jpg?lossy 400w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/qFzr8HQiQ1b1IzFMxiQjj2xRaAM=/800x0/article-new/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-lineup-feature5.jpg?lossy 800w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/SwcfeDJ7Vr5X9trxkhN6pdTAkJ4=/1600x0/article-new/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-lineup-feature5.jpg?lossy 1600w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/gDTtNEZkPadt213LsmdRgjxsdUQ=/2500x0/filters:no_upscale()/article-new/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-lineup-feature5.jpg?lossy 2500w" data-sizes="auto" loading="lazy" style="aspect-ratio:2500/1406" /><noscript><img src="https://images.macrumors.com/article-new/2026/10/Apple-HomeView-lineup-feature5.jpg" alt="Apple HomeView lineup feature5" width="2500" height="1406" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-1070618" /></noscript><br />Apple describes Secure Exclaves as compartmentalized runtimes that process camera and microphone data while isolated from the rest of the operating system. Data processed in Secure Exclaves is not available to the rest of the OS, apps, or Apple, but processing can take advantage of the full application processor. Secure Exclaves power sensitive features involving video and audio feeds:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>HomeView</strong> - The HomeView uses facial and voice recognition to identify up to six people in a home. The exclave also protects the LED camera indicator on the device.</li>
<li><strong>Siri Recap and Live Rewind</strong> - Record ambient sound for conversation recaps or to caption the last 15 seconds of someone speaking.</li>
<li><strong>iPhone 18 Pro/iPhone Duo</strong> - Protects the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌, Pro Max, and Duo on-screen camera and microphone indicators. Also works with "Hey <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/guide/siri/">Siri</a>" to protect voice data.</li>
<li><strong>MacBook Neo</strong> - Protects the <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/macbook-neo/">MacBook Neo</a> camera indicator.</li>
</ul>
<p>Apple uses the HomeView as an example of how Secure Exclaves work. The device performs passive minimal visual processing continually to detect whether a person is in its field of view. The HomeView sends a continuous stream of camera frames to a camera exclave, which works alongside a person recognition exclave with face and voice recognition models and an identity database. When a person comes into view, the camera exclave detects the person and lets the main OS know that a person may be present, but no image data leaves the Secure Exclave. An audio exclave does the same thing with audio.</p>
<p>The person recognition exclave matches face and voice prints against the identity database of enrolled users, giving a confidence score. The OS gets the person identifier, position, and confidence level, but not any of the actual audio or video. These simple signals are used to activate personal features like Calendar and Messages that depend on identity, with raw sensor data discarded.</p>
<p>Secure Exclaves came about because Apple needed a secure option for ambient video and microphone monitoring, with the groundwork laid starting in iOS 18. Apple devices use indicators for situations where the camera and microphone are actively engaged, but Apple says they weren't ideal for ambient sensing because they would be on all the time. Always-on lights wouldn't give users a way to distinguish between background sensing and active audio and video recording.</p>
<p>There are two modes for a Secure Exclave: ambient mode and active mode. In ambient mode with no indicator, a sensor can respond to triggers, but it only shares small amounts of metadata with the rest of the system. In active mode, full sensor data is given to the operating system, and an indicator informs the user that the system has audio and video access.</p>
<p>Apple has long used indicators, but they are now backed by Secure Exclaves. Secure Exclaves make sure an indicator is active before data is allowed to be transferred from the exclave to the rest of the OS.</p>
<p>Apple built an isolated computing environment that could handle ambient sensing, and the company says isolating memory for Secure Exclaves was a "serious engineering challenge." Full technical details on the process <a href="https://security.apple.com/blog/secure-exclaves/">can be found on Apple's security website</a>.</p>

<p><img alt="apple homeview on black" width="2500" height="1406" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-1071345 lazyload" src="https://images.macrumors.com/images-new/1x1.trans.gif" data-src="https://images.macrumors.com/t/TWriTSblcoU0hqQ7NJxEkfSaWDI=/400x0/article-new/2026/10/apple-homeview-on-black.jpeg?lossy" data-srcset="https://images.macrumors.com/t/TWriTSblcoU0hqQ7NJxEkfSaWDI=/400x0/article-new/2026/10/apple-homeview-on-black.jpeg?lossy 400w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/O_oO5ea8_OjFM4gPr3q95pV3gRk=/800x0/article-new/2026/10/apple-homeview-on-black.jpeg?lossy 800w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/9Cgdwrq7UxrzE3fOne9FfVCmTVg=/1600x0/article-new/2026/10/apple-homeview-on-black.jpeg?lossy 1600w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/UjSzP3xmHgpwuyoupRfK4m-CJ_I=/2500x0/filters:no_upscale()/article-new/2026/10/apple-homeview-on-black.jpeg?lossy 2500w" data-sizes="auto" loading="lazy" style="aspect-ratio:2500/1406" /><noscript><img src="https://images.macrumors.com/article-new/2026/10/apple-homeview-on-black.jpeg" alt="apple homeview on black" width="2500" height="1406" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-1071345" /></noscript><br />The software has a build number of 24V526, and it is the second 27.2 update Apple has released for the device.</p>
<p>Customers receiving the HomeView this week will need to install a software update during the setup process. The HomeView ships with <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/01/apple-homeview-six-month-old-software/">HomeView Software 26.5</a>, which is approximately six months old.</p>
<p>Apple planned to release the HomeView earlier than November 2026 but held back because it wanted to debut <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/guide/siri/">Siri</a> AI in <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/ios-27/">iOS 27</a> first.</p>
<p>Apple today said it plans to <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/12/apple-plans-homeview-update-with-siri-fix/">release a HomeView software update</a> to fix a ‌Siri‌ AI issue that prevents ‌Siri‌ from controlling smart home products like locks, but that update isn't coming until next month. It's likely the ‌Siri‌ AI issue will be addressed in HomeView 27.3.</p>
<p><b>Update:</b> Apple's <a href="https://support.apple.com/en-us/149851">security support document</a> says the software update addresses several vulnerabilities, including issues with <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/guide/airplay/">AirPlay</a>, Messages, and Bluetooth.</p>

The iPhone 17 Pro Max falls $30 to $855, while the iPhone Air and standard iPhone 17 each gain $30, bringing both to $615.</p>
<p>Many older models recover some of the value lost in <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/09/15/apple-cuts-iphone-trade-in-value/">September's reductions</a>. Most remain below their pre-September maximums, although the second-generation iPhone SE returns to $45, fully reversing its $5 cut.</p>
<p>The following iPhone estimates have changed. Each price is the maximum available trade-in credit:<br />

<ul>

<p>For customers switching from Android, Apple has added six Samsung foldables to its trade-in list. The Galaxy Z Fold7 receives the highest maximum offer among the additions, while the Galaxy Z Flip5 has the lowest:<br />
</p>
<ul>
<li>Samsung Galaxy Z Fold7: <strong>$410</strong> (newly listed)</li>

<li>Samsung Galaxy Z Flip5: <strong>$125</strong> (newly listed)</li>
</ul>
<p>Google Pixel owners generally receive lower offers under the update. The Pixel 9 loses $20, the largest dollar reduction among the affected Pixel models, while the Pixel 7 gains $5. The changed maximum estimates are as follows:<br />

<p>The Apple Watch's adjustments are limited to six models. The Apple Watch Ultra 2 gains $10, three other watches gain $5 each, and the original Apple Watch Ultra and Series 7 each lose $5:<br />

<li>Apple Watch Series 6: <strong>$45</strong> (previously $40)</li>
</ul>
<p>Mac and iPad trade-in values stay at the levels <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/26/apple-raises-ipad-and-mac-trade-in-values/">introduced in October</a>, including maximum estimates of $2,560 for the Mac Pro and $915 for the iPad Pro.</p>
<p>Apple also introduced <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/09/09/apple-to-offer-better-trade-in-pricing/">more detailed condition grading</a> in September, improving offers for devices with minor cosmetic defects that previously received deductions similar to those applied to more serious damage.</p>
<p>Actual trade-in offers depend on the device's condition, year, and configuration. Through <a href="https://www.apple.com/shop/trade-in">Apple Trade In</a>, eligible devices can be exchanged for credit toward a purchase or an Apple Gift Card, while devices without trade-in value can be recycled for free.</p>

Nvidia has appointed its CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO.</p>
<p>Nvidia's board of directors has initiated a search for a new CEO and said that it will consider both internal and external candidates.</p>
<p>Cook stepped down as Apple's CEO on September 1 as part of <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/04/20/tim-cook-stepping-down/">a planned transition</a>, and he now serves as the company's executive chairman.</p>
<p>There is no indication that Cook actually wants to be Nvidia's CEO.</p>
<p><em>Semafor</em> on Wednesday reported that Apple's longtime chipmaking chief Johny Srouji is <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/12/johny-srouji-eyed-as-potential-nvidia-ceo/">among the people that Nvidia is considering for CEO</a>, but it is likewise unclear if Srouji has any interest in the role. Srouji was <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/04/20/srouji-chief-hardware-officer/">named Apple's Chief Hardware Officer</a> in April, at the same time as Apple announced John Ternus would become its next CEO.</p>

href="https://www.nintendo.com/au/support/articles/discontinuation-of-google-and-apple-accounts-linking-to-nintendo-accounts/">announced</a>.</p>
<p><img alt="sign in with apple" width="1200" height="675" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-1077071 lazyload" src="https://images.macrumors.com/images-new/1x1.trans.gif" data-src="https://images.macrumors.com/t/Tq3XNq56okBdO9x1AnIp3PM0s-M=/400x0/article-new/2026/11/sign-in-with-apple.jpeg?lossy" data-srcset="https://images.macrumors.com/t/Tq3XNq56okBdO9x1AnIp3PM0s-M=/400x0/article-new/2026/11/sign-in-with-apple.jpeg?lossy 400w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/W_Ly5adLHdmB8wloGFgeQ26zI3U=/800x0/article-new/2026/11/sign-in-with-apple.jpeg?lossy 800w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/YqNTnHVN9Z5fbuWRl8ZI8qF5Nc8=/1600x0/article-new/2026/11/sign-in-with-apple.jpeg?lossy 1600w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/u-IUV-FWLl1gGixj86TWVYLHX_w=/2500x0/filters:no_upscale()/article-new/2026/11/sign-in-with-apple.jpeg?lossy 2500w" data-sizes="auto" loading="lazy" style="aspect-ratio:1200/675" /><noscript><img src="https://images.macrumors.com/article-new/2026/11/sign-in-with-apple.jpeg" alt="sign in with apple" width="1200" height="675" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-1077071" /></noscript><br />Users will also no longer be able to create a Nintendo Account through either service. Nintendo has not explained why it is removing the options, but notes that the exact cutoff could be delayed depending on the progress of its system updates.</p>
<p>After the change, users will need to sign in with their Nintendo Account email address or Sign-In ID and password, or use a passkey. Nintendo says users who are already signed in on a device may not need to sign in again immediately.</p>
<p>Anyone who usually signs in through Apple or Google should check that they know their Nintendo Account login details before the deadline. Those who have never set a password, or have forgotten it, can select "Forgot your password?" on the <a href="https://accounts.nintendo.com/">Nintendo Account login page</a> to request a reset email.</p>
<p>Users who chose to hide their email address with <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/guide/sign-in-with-apple/">Sign in with Apple</a> may have an Apple-generated relay address registered with Nintendo. Messages sent to that address are forwarded to their personal inbox. Nintendo advises anyone who can no longer access their registered email address to contact its support team.</p>
<p>Nintendo also recommends registering a passkey, which allows users to sign in using their device's fingerprint or facial recognition system instead of a password. The My Nintendo Platinum Points mission for linking a Google account will be discontinued as part of the change.</p>

<p>As a refresher, the HomeView features a 7-inch square display connected to an aluminum speaker base by a stainless steel tilting hinge. Apple says it is ideal for a kitchen counter, nightstand, or side table. You can use the device to interact with Siri AI, control smart home accessories, go on FaceTime video calls, listen to music, and more.</p>
<p>Preinstalled apps on the HomeView include Alarms, Calendar, FaceTime, Find My, Home, Intercom, Messages, Music, Podcasts, Reminders, Safari, Settings, Timers, Weather, and World Clock. The device does not have an App Store, but it does support CarPlay-enabled audio and video apps, such as Apple TV, Spotify, and Apple Music Classical.</p>
<p>In the U.S., both the tabletop and wall-mounted versions of the HomeView are priced at $299, but you will also need to purchase a mount if you opt for the wall-mounted version. Apple sells three mounts priced between $59.95 and $129.95.</p>

<p><img alt="apple home collection feature2" width="2500" height="1406" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-1070669 lazyload" src="https://images.macrumors.com/images-new/1x1.trans.gif" data-src="https://images.macrumors.com/t/D0Dh-JyPyDYPGYm2kWOoiSMYuWA=/400x0/article-new/2026/10/apple-home-collection-feature2.jpg?lossy" data-srcset="https://images.macrumors.com/t/D0Dh-JyPyDYPGYm2kWOoiSMYuWA=/400x0/article-new/2026/10/apple-home-collection-feature2.jpg?lossy 400w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/t2gLaCDa-o2v-HWxCzB0N0CWRig=/800x0/article-new/2026/10/apple-home-collection-feature2.jpg?lossy 800w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/Gamfzq6EH6ErC5Ay_Paz6EJvQsA=/1600x0/article-new/2026/10/apple-home-collection-feature2.jpg?lossy 1600w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/0I_eTIQrr74zIGikqmDVo4KHhzs=/2500x0/filters:no_upscale()/article-new/2026/10/apple-home-collection-feature2.jpg?lossy 2500w" data-sizes="auto" loading="lazy" style="aspect-ratio:2500/1406" /><noscript><img src="https://images.macrumors.com/article-new/2026/10/apple-home-collection-feature2.jpg" alt="apple home collection feature2" width="2500" height="1406" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-1070669" /></noscript><br />Introduced alongside Apple's new <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/13/apple-announces-homeview-smart-home-hub/">HomeView</a> smart home hub last month, the Apple Home Collection is a new lineup of smart home accessories that LG and Schneider Electric designed in collaboration with Apple. There are indoor and outdoor cameras, thermostats, temperature sensors, a video doorbell, and a door lock.</p>
<p>All of the Apple Home Collection accessories work with the HomeView:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>LG Video Doorbell ($249.95)</strong> - The Video Doorbell has dual cameras that capture views of visitors and packages. The front camera has a 2.5K resolution and the bottom camera is full HD resolution. It has a built-in spotlight and a chime that plays through HomeView, HomePod, or HomePod mini.</li>
<li><strong>LG Outdoor Cam ($299.95)</strong> - The Outdoor Cam has low-light color night vision and can be angled in multiple positions.</li>
<li><strong>LG Indoor Cam ($199.95)</strong> - The Indoor Cam has a privacy-preserving feature that allows it to tilt up when people are in the home so it's not recording, and down when people leave for keeping an eye on the home. The tilt function works based on geofencing, but can also be controlled in the Home app or manually.</li>
<li><strong>LG Floodlight Cam ($399.95)</strong> - The Floodlight Cam has dual floodlights that activate when motion is detected and low-light color night vision.</li>
<li><strong>LG Smart Deadbolt Lock ($349.95)</strong> - The lock has Ultra Wideband and can unlock automatically when the homeowner approaches, with no tap required. It also supports unlocking via PIN or a hidden backup key slot, and there is detection for whether the door is opened, closed, or has been tampered with. The doorbell and lock can work together as one, letting users see who is at the door and unlocking it if needed.</li>
<li><strong>LG Thermostat ($199.95)</strong> - The thermostat supports Adaptive Temperature and in the U.S., heating and cooling can be activated during lower-cost periods for users with a compatible utility plan. The thermostat can read temperature and humidity across multiple rooms using separate temperature and humidity sensors. Sensors are priced at $39.95.</li>
<li><strong>Schneider Electric Thermostat ($199.95)</strong> - Also supports Adaptive Temperature and can be used with temperature and humidity sensors. Sensors are priced at $39.95.</li>
</ul>
<p>For more details about the accessories, read <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/13/apple-home-collection/">our previous coverage</a>.</p>
<p>Apple previously announced that some of the accessories will not be released until early 2027, so not everything will be available to order tomorrow.</p>

minor--3O_9dH4U" data-io-article-url="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/12/johny-srouji-eyed-as-potential-nvidia-ceo/"><div class="js-contentInner"><p>Apple's chief hardware officer Johny Srouji is being considered as a potential successor to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as the chipmaker's board prepares to remove its co-founder, according to <a href="https://www.semafor.com/article/11/11/2026/nvidia-board-preparing-to-oust-ceo-huang-wsj"><em>Semafor</em></a>.</p>
<p><img alt="johny srouji" width="1600" height="900" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-1077078 lazyload" src="https://images.macrumors.com/images-new/1x1.trans.gif" data-src="https://images.macrumors.com/t/fuw1BZZRRGFSA5Hb3KBQ94GiQ1Y=/400x0/article-new/2026/11/johny-srouji.jpg?lossy" data-srcset="https://images.macrumors.com/t/fuw1BZZRRGFSA5Hb3KBQ94GiQ1Y=/400x0/article-new/2026/11/johny-srouji.jpg?lossy 400w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/pKNPWH-JywwxPrECuAEPD8_K4Ak=/800x0/article-new/2026/11/johny-srouji.jpg?lossy 800w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/m1Dr4MpdPQ-4uxMzCbxPXs1ZCGE=/1600x0/article-new/2026/11/johny-srouji.jpg?lossy 1600w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/p2DS-v9bznsChMUcnbZrV7OglXI=/2500x0/filters:no_upscale()/article-new/2026/11/johny-srouji.jpg?lossy 2500w" data-sizes="auto" loading="lazy" style="aspect-ratio:1600/900" /><noscript><img src="https://images.macrumors.com/article-new/2026/11/johny-srouji.jpg" alt="johny srouji" width="1600" height="900" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-1077078" /></noscript><br />Citing a person familiar with the matter, the publication identified Srouji as one of the people under consideration for Nvidia's top job. It is unclear if Srouji has yet been approached or expressed interest in leaving Apple.</p>
<p>Nvidia has reportedly hired an outside firm to identify potential replacements for Huang, according to <a href="https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-12/nvidia-drama-triggers-difficult-search-for-huang-s-successor"><em>Bloomberg</em></a>. The succession discussions follow reports of multiple extramarital affairs involving Huang, including one with a woman reportedly suspected of spying for China. Some directors apparently favor appointing chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO if Huang is removed.</p>
<p>Srouji's emergence as a possible candidate comes just months after a substantial expansion of his responsibilities at Apple. In April, Apple <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/04/20/srouji-chief-hardware-officer/">promoted him</a> from senior vice president of hardware technologies to chief hardware officer alongside the announcement that John Ternus would <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/04/20/tim-cook-stepping-down/">succeed Tim Cook</a> as CEO. Srouji took over the hardware engineering organization previously led by Ternus while retaining oversight of Apple's custom chips and other hardware technologies.</p>
<p>The promotion followed uncertainty about Srouji's future at Apple. In December 2025, <em>Bloomberg</em>'s <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/guide/mark-gurman/">Mark Gurman</a> reported that Srouji had told Cook he was <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2025/12/07/SROUJI-COULD-BE-NEXT-TO-GO-AS-EXODUS-CONTINUES/">seriously considering leaving</a> for another company. Cook was reportedly trying to retain him with increased compensation and broader responsibilities. Srouji subsequently <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2025/12/08/johny-srouji-provides-career-update/">told employees</a> that he did not plan to leave "anytime soon."</p>
<p>Srouji helped lead the Mac's <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2022/04/18/apple-silicon-johny-srouji-interview/">transition to Apple silicon</a>, and his hardware technologies organization also oversees areas including cellular modems, cameras, displays, sensors, and batteries. Srouji joined Apple in 2008 to lead development of the A4 chip after holding senior processor development and design roles at Intel and IBM. He was also reportedly <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2019/01/15/johny-srouji-intel-ceo-candidate/">considered for Intel's CEO position</a> in 2019, although that role ultimately <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2019/01/31/intel-names-robert-swan-ceo/">went to Bob Swan</a>.</p>
